solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tramp's flat disgusting externally internally

indicators.note: says the pair of outer letters goes inside the synonym for flat

parts.note: flat in the sense of level or straight, as a true surface is

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word disgusting are the ones wanted here

explanation.surface: A vagrant's apartment is revolting inside and out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' is a verb, and the 's stands for 'is'. 'externally' takes DG from disgusting; 'internally' puts DG inside TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily and wearily, which is exactly what plodding along means.

clue.text: Reduce strain on cause of pain in parts of foot

indicators.note: something that causes pain hurts or wrenches, signalling the letters are twisted into a new order
reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the word strain is dropped

explanation.surface: Advice to ease the stress on whatever is making your feet ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduce' trims STRAIN to STRAI, and 'cause of pain' rearranges those letters. 'on' is a link; the blogger was unsure of the anagram signal too.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the clusters of small bones forming the ankle and back of each foot.

clue.text: Release a local jerk

parts.note: 'un is dialect, a local form, for one or a
a hitch is a sudden jerk or tug

explanation.surface: A villager's sudden tug sets something free.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to unfasten a horse or trailer, freeing it.

clue.text: Controlling last third of active service in progress

indicators.note: says these letters go inside the word for progress

parts.note: going means progressing, under way

indicators.note: the final two of the six letters of the word active

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, an armed service

explanation.surface: Commanding the final phase of an ongoing military tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Governing a country means being in charge of it and directing its affairs.

clue.text: Monk once wanting sex after that woman married

indicators.note: sex is placed after the other pieces, at the end of the answer

parts.note: that woman is her
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A former monk lacked intimacy once that lady wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is only a link, meaning lacking. 'after' places the coy word for sex at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Early Christian monks often lived alone in the desert as recluses, so a solitary religious figure of old fits.

clue.text: Catch-22 author uncovered name — one MacArthur

indicators.note: with its covers off the surname loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Joseph Heller wrote the novel Catch-22

explanation.surface: Revealing the name of a novelist alongside a general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MacArthur' suggests General Douglas, but it is Dame Ellen MacArthur, the British round-the-world yachtswoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen MacArthur is the British sailor who set a solo round-the-world record in 2005.

clue.text: Mass map makers on one type of the other broken ground in Glencoe?

parts.note: M is the physics abbreviation for mass
OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national map makers
'the other' is British slang for sex, and shag is a crude word for it

explanation.surface: Mass-produced maps placed on a cheeky romp in the Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Glencoe is a Highland glen, flagging a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A moss-hag is a Scots term for a hollow or pit in a peat bog, rough broken moorland.

clue.text: Brief hint — album is corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoiled and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A tip that a music album is damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch or description is a short, concise one.

clue.text: Unintroduced demo currently playing out of large record store

indicators.note: losing its introduction means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for large is taken away from the word

parts.note: a show that is currently playing is live
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A demo track being played live outside a big record shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unintroduced' cuts the M from MARCH to give ARCH; 'out of' takes L from LIVE to leave IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection where historical documents and records are kept.

clue.text: Heal completely, nearly getting out of bed

parts.note: close means nearly, as in close to finishing
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A patient almost recovered and ready to leave the sickbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound is said to close up when its edges knit together as it mends fully.

clue.text: Fail to embrace anything pleasurable, as abuser does

indicators.note: says the word for failing wraps around the pleasure

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit
a treat is anything pleasurable

explanation.surface: An abuser denies others any pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abuses others treats them badly, which is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: One holding a flush, clubs and one ace being put in order

indicators.note: says the card letters are placed inside the water tank

parts.note: a cistern is the tank that holds the water for a toilet flush
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
I is the Roman numeral for one
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A card player holding a flush, sorting clubs and an ace into order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One holding a flush' looks like poker talk but means a toilet tank; CIA goes inside it, between CISTER and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cistercians are a monastic order of monks founded at Citeaux in France.

clue.text: Bum — there! — someone's smells

parts.note: ho is a cry drawing attention, like 'there!' or 'land ho!'
BO is body odour, the smell a person gives off

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone's rear and their pong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' is the American sense, a vagrant, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a bum is a homeless wanderer, the same as a tramp who rides the rails.

clue.text: Muslim leader out to lunch eating hot starter from Indian

indicators.note: says the word for crazy takes the letter for hot inside it

parts.note: someone out to lunch is crazy, mad
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Indian is used

explanation.surface: A religious leader away at lunch, tucking into a spicy Indian starter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic belief the Mahdi is the prophesied redeemer who will lead the faithful before the end of time.

clue.text: Lovely Rita, setting an example, tailed woman penning note

indicators.note: says the woman encloses the musical note

parts.note: a mermaid is a woman with a fish's tail
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A lovely girl showing the way, a woman with a ponytail writing a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovely Rita' is the Beatles song about a traffic warden, 'Lovely Rita, meter maid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter maid is a female traffic warden, and the Beatles' Rita is one.

clue.text: With runners, ride horse over on soggy ground to opening

indicators.note: says the word to comes at the beginning of the answer
the reversed horse is written on, after, the bog

parts.note: a bog is soggy ground

indicators.note: turned over means the word for horse is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A horse rider going over boggy ground to reach a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With runners' points to a sled, not racehorses. 'over' turns NAG into GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a sled on runners, and as a verb it means to slide downhill on one.

clue.text: Billed one male — female concerned with children

parts.note: a bull is a male animal
in can mean involved or concerned with, as in 'in shipping'

explanation.surface: A man and woman charged in a case concerning children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billed' means having a beak, not invoiced.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullfinch is a songbird with a short stout beak, so a creature with a bill.

clue.text: Stray American replacing uniform in conflict

indicators.note: says the American letter takes the place of the uniform letter

parts.note: a struggle is a conflict
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A US soldier goes AWOL from the war, swapping out his uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: To straggle is to wander off or fall behind the main group, much as a stray does.

clue.text: Case for admission, chest not over deadly disease

indicators.note: the outside letters, the case, of the word admission
says the letter for over is left out of the word for chest

parts.note: the thorax is the chest
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A patient admitted with a chest complaint that turns out fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthrax is a serious bacterial infection of livestock and people that can kill.

clue.text: Defamation, I'll be damned

indicators.note: damned suggests the letters have been ruined and recast

explanation.surface: Someone slandered exclaims in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is false and damaging statement about someone, published in writing.

clue.text: Not after compassion off Pat

parts.note: by means not later than, as in 'by noon'
heart is compassion, kindness

explanation.surface: Someone seeking sympathy, not from Pat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off Pat' looks like 'away from Pat' but is the phrase 'off pat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing something off pat means having it memorised perfectly.

clue.text: Young fish dash across river

indicators.note: says the word for dash stretches across, around, the river letter

parts.note: a dash is a little bit, as of milk
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A small fish darting over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Brit is the young of the herring and similar fish, swimming in shoals.

clue.text: Is he almost past being this unhealthy?

definitions.text: Is he almost past being this unhealthy?

parts.words: Is he almost past being this unhealthy?
parts.note: someone almost past it, nearly over the hill, is likely to be in poor physical condition

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an unfit man is nearly over the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in poor physical condition, unfit, is the everyday idiom for lacking fitness.

clue.text: Force losing black cat

indicators.note: says the letter for black is dropped from the word

parts.note: to bounce someone into something is to force or pressure them
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A police force losing a black cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big wild feline.

clue.text: Former prince covering up endless debauchery

indicators.note: says the prince letters go around the shortened word, hiding it
says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a riot is wild revelry, debauchery

explanation.surface: An ex-royal hushing up his wild carousing.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier or previous, as in a prior engagement.

clue.text: Uncertain against a let

parts.note: V is short for versus, against
to let is to grant or allow

explanation.surface: Someone unsure, arguing against renting out a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagrant can describe something wandering and inconstant, so unsettled and unpredictable.

clue.text: Head briefly around salt lake, for one

indicators.note: says the shortened head goes around the sailor
cut short means the last letter of the slang word is dropped

parts.note: onion is slang for the head
a salt is an old sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: A man ducks his head beside a salt lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt lake' looks like one phrase but splits: salt is the sailor, and 'lake, for one' is the definition. 'briefly' drops the head's last letter; 'around' wraps what is left round the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes of North America, so a lake is an example.

clue.text: On the right-hand side and a little lower

definitions.meaning: the heraldic and Latin word for the right side
a small breed of cattle, and a cow is something that lows

explanation.surface: Directions for hanging a picture slightly lower and to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is something that moos, not a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter means on the right in heraldry, and Dexter cattle are a famously small Irish breed of cow.

clue.text: Trace with a ruler — it's more reliable

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, a trace
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, a ruler

explanation.surface: Drawing a line with a ruler gives a more dependable result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' is a monarch, not a straight edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiter can mean more honest or upright, as in whiter than white, so more trustworthy.
